name: Dabigatran etexilate
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: CrCl >30: 150 mg twice daily; CrCl 15–30: 75 mg twice daily

usual_adult_dose.indication: DVT/PE treatment and prevention of recurrence
usual_adult_dose.dose: 150 mg twice daily (CrCl >30), after 5 to 10 days of parenteral anticoagulation for treatment
110 mg on day 1, then 220 mg once daily (CrCl >30)

key_interactions.effect: Higher exposure, especially with kidney impairment (label).
key_interactions.action: AF, CrCl 30–50: 75 mg twice daily; CrCl <30: avoid; VTE, CrCl <50: avoid.

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Antiplatelets, NSAIDs, heparin, fibrinolytics, other anticoagulants
key_interactions.action: Avoid unnecessary combinations; watch for bleeding.

common: Dyspepsia, gastritis-like symptoms, nausea, upper abdominal pain
serious: Thrombotic events after premature discontinuation (boxed warning)
Spinal or epidural hematoma with neuraxial procedures (boxed warning)
Thrombosis with mechanical heart valves or triple-positive antiphospholipid syndrome

monitoring: Before procedures: stop 1–2 days ahead (CrCl ≥50) or 3–5 days (CrCl <50) (label 2.8)

pk.metabolism: Esterase hydrolysis of the prodrug; glucuronidation; not CYP

sources.citation: Boehringer Ingelheim Pharmaceuticals Inc. (2025). PRADAXA (dabigatran etexilate) capsules [Prescribing information; US FDA-approved label, NDA022512, set ID ba74e3cd-b06f-4145-b284-5fd6b84ff3c9, version effective June 25, 2025]. DailyMed, U.S. National Library of Medicine.

Schwartz, G. J., Muñoz, A., Schneider, M. F., Mak, R. H., Kaskel, F., Warady, B. A., & Furth, S. L. (2009). New equations to estimate GFR in children with CKD. Journal of the American Society of Nephrology, 20(3), 629–637.

revision_log.change: Pre-procedure stop times (label 2.8) added to monitoring.
